patterns.usage_note: Carries an action through to completion, very often coloring it with regret or irreversibility: it is done and cannot be taken back (財布を忘れてしまった, 全部やっちゃった). The bare past た merely reports the event, and 〜ておく frames the act as deliberate groundwork. ちゃう and じゃう are colloquial contractions of てしまう/でしまう; じゃう goes on the verbs whose te-form is で, that is ぐ verbs (泳いじゃう) and む/ぬ/ぶ verbs (読んじゃう).

examples.ruby: 電車[でんしゃ]に財布[さいふ]を忘[わす]れてしまった。
examples.english: I went and left my wallet on the train.

examples.ruby: 宿題[しゅくだい]はもう全部[ぜんぶ]やっちゃったよ。
examples.english: I've already knocked out all my homework.

examples.ruby: 牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]を一気[いっき]に飲[の]んじゃいました。
examples.english: I went and downed the milk in one go.

glosses: do … and leave it that way (for later)
patterns.usage_note: Does something ahead of time, or leaves a result standing for later use, so the act is inherently deliberate (お茶を入れておきました, 窓は開けておいてください). That is the line between it and 〜てしまう, whose completion is often unintended, and the neutral past た. It describes the preparer's action, whereas 〜てある describes the state that action left behind. Casual speech contracts it to とく/どく (読んどく, 冷やしとく).

examples.ruby: 遠足[えんそく]の朝[あさ]、水筒[すいとう]にお茶[ちゃ]を入[い]れておきました。
examples.english: On the morning of the field trip I filled my flask with tea before we set off.

examples.ruby: ビールは冷[ひ]やしといたから、遠慮[えんりょ]しないでね。
examples.english: I've got the beer chilling, so help yourself.

examples.ruby: 暑[あつ]いので窓[まど]は開[あ]けておいてください。
examples.english: It's hot, so please leave the window open.

patterns.usage_note: Plain た/だ marks a completed event or state and simply reports that it happened (昨日友達に会った), without the regret of てしまった or the preparation of ておいた. だ is the same ending on verbs whose te-form takes で, that is ぐ・む・ぬ・ぶ verbs (泳いだ、読んだ、選んだ). The separate 並立 item だの is unrelated: it strings complaints together (高いだのまずいだの). た also does non-past work, discovery (あ、ここにあった) and brisk commands (どいた、どいた).

examples.ruby: 昨日[きのう]は公園[こうえん]で古[ふる]い友人[ゆうじん]に会[あ]った。
examples.english: Yesterday I ran into an old friend at the park.

examples.ruby: 朝[あさ]ごはんを食[た]べてから出[で]かけた。
examples.english: I had breakfast and then headed out.

examples.ruby: 妹[いもうと]は迷[まよ]わず、一番[いちばん]大[おお]きなケーキを選[えら]んだ。
examples.english: My little sister went straight for the biggest piece of cake.
